questions.stem: Which OWASP category includes SQL injection and command injection?
questions.explanation: OWASP A03:2021, Injection covers all flaws where attacker input is interpreted as code or commands by an interpreter.

questions.stem: Parameterised queries prevent SQL injection by:

choices.B: Escaping all single quotes in user input
choices.D: Separating SQL code from data at the protocol level so input is never interpreted as SQL syntax

questions.explanation: Parameterised queries pass user input as typed data parameters. The database driver never treats them as SQL syntax, making injection structurally impossible.

choices.A: Scripts are stored in a database and served to other users
choices.B: An attacker runs scripts on the backend server
choices.C: User input is reflected in an HTML response without sanitisation, executing in the victim's browser
choices.D: JavaScript is injected into HTTP headers

questions.explanation: Reflected XSS reflects attacker input directly into the HTML response. A victim who loads the crafted URL executes the injected script in their browser.

choices.A: Execution of JavaScript from any domain
choices.B: Caching of authenticated pages for offline use
choices.C: Trust of JavaScript from the same subdomain
choices.D: Inclusion of session cookies with all requests to a matching domain, enabling forged authenticated requests

questions.explanation: CSRF forges requests by exploiting automatic cookie inclusion. A malicious page can submit authenticated requests to a bank where the victim is logged in.

questions.stem: A Content Security Policy (CSP) header primarily mitigates:

choices.B: CSRF by validating the Referer header
choices.C: XSS by restricting which script sources the browser is permitted to load and execute
choices.D: Path traversal by blocking directory navigation

questions.explanation: CSP defines trusted origins for scripts and other resources. Injected inline scripts and scripts from attacker-controlled origins are blocked by the browser.

choices.A: Inject SQL into file upload parameters
choices.B: Execute JavaScript outside the current page context
choices.C: Navigate to parent directories outside the web root to access sensitive system files

questions.explanation: Path traversal navigates the directory tree via '../' to access files outside the web root, such as /etc/passwd or web.config.

questions.stem: SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery) allows an attacker to:

choices.B: Cause the application server to make requests to internal resources unreachable from the internet
choices.C: Submit forged requests in another user's name
choices.D: Inject server-side scripts into database queries

questions.explanation: SSRF makes the server send requests on the attacker's behalf to internal services, metadata APIs, internal databases, that external attackers cannot reach directly.

choices.D: Clickjacking attacks that overlay a malicious frame over a legitimate site

questions.explanation: X-Frame-Options: DENY prevents the browser from rendering the page in any iframe, blocking clickjacking attacks.

questions.stem: Secure Development Lifecycle (SDL) integrates security into:

choices.D: Every phase from requirements through design, coding, testing, and deployment

questions.explanation: SDL/DevSecOps embeds security at every development phase. Finding and fixing vulnerabilities early is far cheaper than remediating in production.

choices.A: Employees to fix internal security bugs
choices.B: External researchers to responsibly report vulnerabilities in exchange for recognition or payment
choices.D: Penetration testers on a crowdsourced basis

questions.explanation: Bug bounty programmes expand security testing coverage by engaging the broader researcher community to find vulnerabilities internal teams miss.
